headline: Carlo Paalam Reaches Asian Games Semifinals, Assures Bronze
seoTitle: Carlo Paalam Reaches Asian Games Semifinals, Assures Bronze | FMB News
seoDescription: Carlo Paalam beat China's Zhang Jiamao 3-2 to reach the Asian Games men's 55kg semifinals and assure the Philippines of at least bronze.
deck: Paalam defeated China’s Zhang Jiamao by 3-2 split decision to reach the men’s 55kg semifinals, guaranteeing at least a bronze medal.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Carlo Paalam defeated China's Zhang Jiamao by split decision, 3-2, in the men's 55kg quarterfinals of the 2026 Asian Games on Monday at Nishio Gymnasium in Japan.
The victory sends Paalam to the semifinals and assures the Philippines of at least a bronze medal because both losing semifinalists receive bronze.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Paalam had reached the quarterfinals after a 3-0 points victory over India's Jadumani Singh Mandengbam in the Round of 16.
An assured bronze is not yet a final medal color. Paalam can still advance to the gold-medal bout with a semifinal victory.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: The result adds another guaranteed podium finish to the Philippine campaign and gives the Tokyo Olympic silver medalist another chance to improve on his previous Asian Games bronze.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Paalam's semifinal opponent and bout schedule should be confirmed through the official results service. His final medal color remains unresolved until that bout is completed.

verificationNotes: The Game recorded Paalam's 3-2 split-decision quarterfinal win over Zhang Jiamao and semifinal qualification.
One Sports independently reported Paalam's quarterfinal victory.
The official Aichi-Nagoya results index was opened; its event tables require JavaScript and did not expose a text scorecard in this verification environment.
The article says assured bronze, not final bronze, because Paalam remains in contention.
No publisher-owned photograph was reused; the FMB-owned editorial fallback is explicitly non-documentary.
